κύκλῳ κατέ λαμψεν.
3 Ἰδέ μοι, ἀγαπητέ, τὴν βασιλεύουσαν Ῥώμην σταυροῦ συμ-βόλοις ἐν μέσῳ
τῆς ἀγορᾶς σεμνυνομένην. Ἰδέ μοι Παῦλον ἀθα νάτους ἐπιστολὰς συγγραφόμενον
καὶ δοῦλον τοῦ σταυροῦ ἑαυ τὸν καταγράψαντα· οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη τὸν σταυρόν, τὸ
σκάν δαλον τῶν Ἰουδαίων· τὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν μω ρίαν σοφίας ἐπεσπάσατο
φυλακτήριον· ἐν σταυροῦ ξύλῳ τὰς τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐκκλησίας διήγειρεν. Μία
ῥάβδος μωσαϊκὴ τὰς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων μάστιγας ἀπήλασεν, ῥάβδος δὲ συγ γενείᾳ πρὸς
τὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ ξύλον παύει τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἁ μαρτήματα. Ἐκεῖ Φαραὼ
καταποντοῦται τὸν Ἰσραὴλ καταδιώκων, ἐνταῦθα δὲ διάβολος καταλύεται, οἱ δὲ τοῦ
σωτῆρος προσκυνηταὶ σῴζονται. Ἐκεῖ τὰς χεῖρας ἐκτεί νας ὁ Ἀδὰμ θάνατον ἡμῖν
ἐπεσπάσατο, ὁ δὲ ἡμέτερος δεσπότης τῇ τῶν χειρῶν ἐκτάσει τὰ πάντα διέσωσεν.
4 Ἀλλ' ὦ ξύλον μεγαλοπρεπέστερον οὐρανοῦ καὶ τὰς οὐρα νίους ἁψῖδας
ὑπερβάλλον, ὦ ξύλον τρισμακάριστον τὰς ἡμετέρας ψυχὰς διαπορθμεῦον εἰς
οὐρανόν, ὦ ξύλον τῷ κόσμῳ τὴν σωτηρίαν πορισάμενον καὶ στρατὸν διαβολικὸν
ἐκδιῶξαν, ὦ ξύλον λῃστὴν εἰς παράδεισον ἀκοντίσαν καὶ μετὰ Χριστοῦ χορεύειν
πεποιηκός· «Ἀμήν, ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω σοι ὅτι σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.»
thought_title: Rome, Paul, and the Cross as Victory over Egypt and Adam
orientation: Hesychius continues his Paschal homily, now pointing to imperial Rome honoring the cross, Paul's apostolic witness, and a typological contrast between Moses' rod and the cross, Pharaoh and the devil, Adam and Christ.
pass_a_gloss: [In] a circle [it] shone around. 3 Behold to me, beloved, the ruling Rome by [the] cross's symbols in [the] middle of the market-place [being] honored. Behold to me Paul [with] unshakeable letters writing and [a] slave of the cross himself having inscribed; not he was ashamed the cross, the stumbling-block of the Jews; the of the nations folly [of] wisdom he dragged [as] an amulet; in cross's wood the of the inhabited-world churches he roused. One rod Mosaic the of the Egyptians plagues drove away, rod but by nature to the of the cross wood stops the of men sins. There Pharaoh is drowned pursuing Israel, here but devil is destroyed, the but of the savior worshipers are saved. There the hands having stretched out Adam death to us dragged, the but our master by the of the hands stretching all things saved through. 4 But O wood more magnificent [than] heaven and the heavenly heights surpassing, O wood thrice-blessed our souls ferrying into heaven, O wood [for] the world salvation having procured and army devilish having driven out, O wood thief into paradise having hurled and with Christ to dance having made; "Amen, amen for I say to you that today with me you will be in the paradise."

lemmas.gloss: signs, tokens (here: public representations of the cross)
stumbling-block, offense (Paul's term for the cross to Jews)
foolishness (Paul's term for the cross to Gentiles)
safeguard, protective charm (here: the cross as wisdom's guard)
rod, staff (Moses' rod and the cross as a rod)
kinship, affinity (the cross as a rod akin to Moses' rod)
is drowned, sinks into the sea
is undone, destroyed, brought to nothing

choices.term: Ῥώμην σταυροῦ συμβόλοις ἐν μέσῳ τῆς ἀγορᾶς σεμνυνομένην
choices.english: Rome glorified by signs of the cross in the middle of the marketplace
choices.why: Glossary renders συμβόλα τοῦ σταυροῦ as "signs of the cross"; σεμνύνω is "glorify, honor, make venerable"; ἀγορά is marketplace/public square.
rejected: Rome adorned with symbols of the cross
Rome honored by cross tokens in the forum

choices.why: ἀθάνατος = immortal/undying; Paul's epistles are called immortal because they live on. Glossary has no entry; literal sense kept.
φυλακτήριον can mean amulet/safeguard; here the cross as "foolishness to Gentiles" becomes wisdom's protective sign. Glossary: no entry; literal sense kept.

choices.term: ῥάβδος δὲ συγγενείᾳ πρὸς τὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ ξύλον
choices.english: but a rod akin by nature to the wood of the cross
choices.why: συγγένεια = kinship/affinity; the cross is a rod related to Moses' rod. Glossary: σταυρός = the cross; ξύλον = wood (of the cross).
rejected: a rod by kinship to the cross's wood
a rod related by nature to the wood of the cross

choices.why: διάσωζω = save thoroughly, bring safely through; here Christ's outstretched hands save all. Glossary: no entry; force of compound kept.
ἀκοντίζω = throw, hurl, launch (as a javelin); vivid for the thief's sudden entry. Glossary: παραδεῖσος = paradise; λῃστής = robber/thief.

bible_refs.note: Mosaic rod driving off Egypt's plagues
Adam stretching out hands bringing death
«Ἀμήν, ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω σοι ὅτι σήμερον μετ' ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ.»

pass_b_english: Look at imperial Rome, glorified by signs of the cross standing in the middle of its public square. Look at Paul writing immortal letters and describing himself as a slave of the cross. He was not ashamed of the cross, the stumbling-block to the Jews. He seized the foolishness of the Gentiles as a safeguard of wisdom. By the wood of the cross he roused the churches of the inhabited world. One Mosaic rod drove off the plagues of the Egyptians, but a rod akin by nature to the wood of the cross puts an end to human sins. There Pharaoh drowned while pursuing Israel; here the devil is undone, and the worshippers of the Savior are saved. There Adam stretched out his hands and brought death upon us; here our Master, by the stretching out of his hands, saved all things completely. O wood more magnificent than heaven and surpassing the heavenly vaults, O thrice-blessed wood that ferries our souls into heaven, O wood that procured salvation for the world and drove out the demonic host, O wood that launched a robber into paradise and made him dance with Christ: 'Amen, amen, I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.'
notes: Opening fragment κύκλῳ κατέ λαμψεν belongs to previous sentence (Matthew 5:15 allusion: "it gives light to all in the house"); only the tail is visible here.

last_rejected.why: The section opens with a full claim that something shone all around; the English never says it.
last_rejected.fix: It shone all around. Look, beloved, at imperial Rome
last_rejected.ruling: 'κύκλῳ κατέλαμψεν.' is a subjectless tail of the previous section, before the '3' marker. It belongs to the prior chunk's translation, so the omission here isn't a meaning loss.
